memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron: "The Israelites are to camp around the tent of meeting some distance from it, each of them under their standard and holding the banners of their family." - Num 2:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives Moses the plan for how the whole nation is to camp, and everything begins with one central truth: the tent of meeting stands in the middle, and the people gather around it. God's presence was not on the edge of the camp — it was the very heart of it.

Every family knew exactly where they belonged, each under their own banner. There was order, identity, and belonging. But above all, there was a centre — and that centre was God.

This is a picture of how life is meant to be lived. When God is at the centre, everything else finds its right place. Our work, our relationships, our plans, our struggles — they all fall into proper order when God holds the central place. When we push Him to the edge, life quickly loses its shape.

Take a moment to ask honestly: what is at the centre of my life right now? Is it my ambitions, my worries, my comforts — or is it God Himself?

In Christ, God has come to dwell not just among His people but within them by His Spirit (John 14:23). He wants to be the centre of your daily life, not a distant figure you visit occasionally. Let everything today be arranged around Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What or who is truly at the centre of your life?
- What would change if God held the central place today?
- Where have you pushed God to the edges?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, be the centre of my life. Help me to arrange everything I am and everything I do around Your presence. Amen.
